title: MINT: Securely Mitigating Rowhammer with a Minimalist in-DRAM Tracker
problem: In-DRAM Rowhammer mitigation faces two critical constraints: mitigations must synchronize with refresh cycles preventing flexible timing, and the available SRAM for aggressor tracking is limited to only a few bytes per bank.
motivation: Rowhammer attacks pose a critical security threat to DRAM, and in-DRAM solutions offer the potential to defend entirely within the chip without relying on external system mechanisms.
method: MINT employs a single tracking entry per bank with forward-looking probabilistic mitigation: at each refresh cycle, it probabilistically decides which activation in the upcoming interval will be selected for mitigation at the next refresh, rather than tracking past behavior or making current-time probabilistic decisions.
key_novelty: The core insight is that if only one row can be mitigated per refresh, only one row needs to be tracked, achieved through forward-looking probabilistic selection rather than backward-looking aggregation.
contributions: Ultra-low-cost secure in-DRAM tracker requiring only a single entry per bank versus hundreds/thousands in prior designs
Forward-looking probabilistic mitigation strategy providing guaranteed protection against single and double-sided Rowhammer attacks
Derivation and analysis of minimum Rowhammer threshold (TRH*) across all attack patterns with MINT achieving 1482 (356 with RFM)
Analysis of refresh postponement compatibility for low-cost in-DRAM trackers and proposed efficient solutions

metrics.other: TRH* of 1482 (356 with RFM); 1 entry per bank versus 677 for prior counter-based design; within 2x of one-counter-per-row ideal design

baselines: counter-based tracker with 677 entries per bank
limitations: Not discussed in abstract; inherent tradeoff between minimal storage overhead and maximum protection level acknowledged.
